data.name: Kaarim
data.gender_notes: Kaarim is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'karama' which means 'to be generous or do good'. Kaarim is a name given to those who are generous, kind, and benevolent. In the Quran, Allah (SWT) is described as the Most Generous, and those who embody this trait in their character will be rewarded in the hereafter. The name Kaarim carries the meaning “Generous, Generous-hearted” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kaarim usually hope their child will grow to embody generous, generous-hearted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carry the spirit of generosity and kindness with you, reflecting the traits of Allah (SWT).
data.etymology: Kaarim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Generous, Generous-hearted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kaarim total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: كريم
in_arabic.long_meaning: كريم هو اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني العطوف الجميل السخي، وهو من الأسماء التي وردت في القرآن الكريم، مثل قوله تعالى: 'وَيُعَطِفُ مِسْكاً وَيُعَطِفُ كَرِيماً'، ويعبر عن الشخص الذي يتصف بالكرم والجود والعفو

in_urdu.name: کریم
in_urdu.meaning: کریم کا مطلب ہے مہربان خوبصورت فراخدل
in_urdu.long_meaning: کریم ایک عظیم نام ہے جو اسلامی تقویم میں بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے، یہ نام مہربان خوبصورت فراخدل کے معنی میں ہے، جو اللہ تعالیٰ کی خوبصوتیوں میں سے ایک ہے، اور قرآن مجید میں بھی ذکر ہوا ہے

in_hindi.name: करीम
in_hindi.meaning: करीम का अर्थ है दयालु सुंदर उदार
in_hindi.long_meaning: करीम एक पवित्र नाम है जो इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत महत्व रखता है, यह नाम दयालु सुंदर उदार के अर्थ में है, जो अल्लाह की विशेषताओं में से एक है, और कुरआन में भी इसका उल्लेख है

in_english.name: Kaarim
in_english.long_meaning: The name Kaarim originates from Arabic roots, signifying generosity, nobility, and kindness. It is one of the names of Allah in Islam, mentioned in the Quran. Historically, it has been used to describe individuals with noble character and a generous spirit. In Islamic tradition, Kaarim represents a person who embodies compassion, forgiveness, and benevolence

In Muslim communities, this name holds a special place as it encourages individuals to emulate the noble qualities that Allah (SWT) appreciates. It also serves as a daily inspiration for those who bear the name to strive for excellence in their actions, making a positive impact on the people around them.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kaarim serves as a constant reminder of the importance of generosity and kindness in one's character. In Islam, generosity is considered a significant virtue, as it reflects Allah's (SWT) countless blessings upon us. By embodying this trait, a person is not only pleasing Allah but also earns the respect and admiration of those around them. The name Kaarim, therefore, symbolizes a soul that is receptive to Allah's blessings, striving to be a conduit of His blessings to others.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah: Kaarim ibn Abdullah Al-Aqeel was a famous companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and one of the ten promised Paradise. He was known for his generosity and piety. Kaarim was among the earliest converts to Islam and participated in many battles. He was also a close friend and confidant of Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra) and was present during the Battle of Siffin.
historical_references.context: Early Muslim History and Companions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari's Tarikh Al-Rusul Wa Al-Muluk: Kaarim ibn Masruq was a companion of the fourth Caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra) and was known for his piety and kindness. He was one of the few companions who remained loyal to Ali during the civil war following the death of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Kaarim was martyred during the Battle of Nahrawan in 658 AD while defending Ali against the forces of Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan.
historical_references.context: Later Muslim History and Companions of Fourth Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra)
